prompt: Rank these fast-food chains by their 2025 U.S. sales (all restaurants combined), from highest to lowest.
rankLabel: Highest U.S. sales → lowest U.S. sales
explanation: Chick-fil-A sold about $23.9B in the U.S. in 2025, more than Burger King ($11.1B) and KFC ($4.7B) combined, despite having only about 3,300 restaurants and closing on Sundays. It is the No. 3 U.S. chain behind McDonald's ($55.1B) and Starbucks ($30.3B); Taco Bell is No. 4 at $17.2B.

source.title: QSR 50 2026: Top 50 Fast-Food Chains, Ranked by Sales

caveat: Chick-fil-A's figure is a QSR estimate (the company is private), as is Starbucks'; Taco Bell, Burger King and KFC reported theirs. U.S. sales only, so KFC's large international business is not counted.

prompt: As of 2026, rank these clothing and footwear brands by the share of U.S. adults who have a positive opinion of them.
explanation: Levi's is liked by 76% of U.S. adults, ahead of Nike at 67%. Crocs are liked by a majority (54%), and Shein by 36%, although 79% of adults have heard of Shein.

source.title: The most famous clothing & footwear brands (YouGov Ratings)

caveat: YouGov Ratings 'popularity' is the share of all adults with a positive opinion (including people who don't know the brand). Ratings refresh quarterly, so values can shift a point or two.

prompt: In the third quarter of 2026, what share of all U.S. retail sales (in dollars) happened online?
explanation: E-commerce was 17.9% of total U.S. retail sales in the third quarter of 2026 ($347.3B of $1,941.9B, seasonally adjusted). More than four of every five retail dollars were still spent offline.
caveat: Seasonally adjusted (17.2% unadjusted). Total retail includes cars, gasoline and groceries, which are mostly bought in person; excludes restaurants and services.

prompt: In January 2025, what share of U.S. adults had ever used Temu, the low-price shopping app?
explanation: As of January 2025, 44% of U.S. adults had used Temu and 31% had used Shein, according to Morning Consult. Temu only launched in the U.S. in late 2022.
caveat: 'Used' counts any frequency of use. The reading predates the 2025 tariff and de minimis changes; no newer all-adult reading from a comparable pollster was found (a 2026 Omnisend consumer survey reported 58% shopping on Temu in the past year, but its sample is not all adults).

prompt: In August 2025, what percent of U.S. adults said they had heard at least a little about the toy Labubu?
explanation: 47% had heard 'a lot' (15%) or 'a little' (32%) about Labubu; 53% had heard nothing at all. Awareness ran from 74% of adults under 30 to 26% of those 65 and older.
caveat: Sample is U.S. adult citizens; margin of error ±3.8 points.

prompt: In 2025, what share of U.S. adults used a 'buy now, pay later' service (such as Klarna, Affirm or Afterpay) in the past 12 months?
explanation: 16% of adults used buy now, pay later in the prior 12 months, according to the Federal Reserve's 2025 household survey, up from 10% in 2021. About a quarter of those users (26%) paid late at least once.

source.title: Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025: Credit (SHED)

caveat: Self-reported use in the prior 12 months. Industry polls that ask 'ever used' report much higher figures.

prompt: In 2026, what percent of U.S. adults had drunk coffee in the past day?
explanation: 66% of American adults had coffee in the past day in the National Coffee Association's Spring 2026 survey, ahead of bottled water (64%), tea (47%) and soda (46%). The association's Fall 2026 report found the same 66%.

source.title: Coffee Tops Americans' Beverage Choices (Spring 2026 National Coffee Data Trends)

extraSources.title: Two-Thirds of Americans Drank Coffee Yesterday, NCA Report Finds
NCA Newsroom (Fall 2026 National Coffee Data Trends release, Sept. 15, 2026)

caveat: Industry trade-group survey of adults who drank something other than tap water the previous day, so the true all-adult share is very slightly lower. The comparison figures for other drinks are as reported by Daily Coffee News.
